walkthroughs.h2: Electrophilic addition of HBr to propene
walkthroughs.body_html:
Pi electrons of C=C attack H-Br: H added, Br- formed. Carbocation forms on either C; Markovnikov favours more stable 2° cation.

Br- attacks the carbocation -> 2-bromopropane (major). Minor product: 1-bromopropane via 1° cation.

SN1: 2 steps via carbocation; 1st order; favoured by 3° R-X, polar protic solvent. Racemic product possible.

SN2: 1 step concerted; 2nd order; favoured by 1° R-X, polar aprotic solvent. Inversion of configuration.

Haloalkane + ethanolic KOH (heat) -> alkene (elimination). Aqueous KOH -> alcohol (substitution).

Higher temperature and bulkier base favour elimination. Zaitsev's rule: most substituted (stable) alkene predominates.
